summary: onSave is now async. It writes a snapshot of the store to data/notes.json after each save.

findings.title: Async onSave breaks the synchronous dispatch caller
findings.problem: onSave now returns a Promise, and dispatch in src/router.js:7 returns that Promise unchanged. The request handler in src/main.js:9 passes the Promise straight to res.end, which accepts only a string or a Buffer.
findings.consequence: Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE inside the request handler on every POST /save request. That uncaught exception crashes the server process.
findings.fix: Make dispatch async and have the request handler await it. Alternatively, keep onSave synchronous and run the snapshot write as a separate, handled task.

findings.title: Snapshot write rejection is never handled
findings.problem: No caller awaits the Promise from onSave or attaches a catch handler to it. writeFile rejects when the data directory is missing or cannot be written.
findings.consequence: A failed snapshot write becomes an unhandled rejection, and Node exits the server process on unhandled rejections by default.
findings.fix: Await dispatch in the request handler and catch errors there. The catch block should answer with an error status.

findings.title: New snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds a file write and an async return to onSave. No test in the repository exercises onSave.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the save path, like the broken caller above, reach production unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls dispatch with the save action and checks both the response and the snapshot file.
